summary: The Qase agent runtime was failing with 'ENOSPC: no space left on device' because the project's storage volume had completely filled up (0 bytes free). I freed roughly 750 MB so agent workspaces can be created again, and diagnosed a deeper disk corruption problem that needs a support-side repair.
what_was_done: Deleted leftover build archives, comparison folders and stray screenshots from the project directory (~260 MB)
Deleted duplicate browser caches and unused tool caches that were silently eating the same disk as the project (~370 MB)
Moved the browser binaries and agent runtime dependencies to the container's separate large scratch disk so they stop consuming project disk permanently (~700 MB redirected)
Verified the agent can now create its workspace folders again — the exact operation that was failing now succeeds
Confirmed the Qase web app still loads normally in the browser
what_was_tested: Creating the exact agent workspace folder that previously failed with ENOSPC — now succeeds
Playwright browser launches from its new location — Chrome 151 starts fine
The agent CLI binary still runs from its relocated dependencies — version check passes
The Qase preview site responds with HTTP 200

test_results.name: Agent workspace folder creation (.qase/workspaces/...)
test_results.note: The exact path from the error message now creates successfully

test_results.name: Browser runtime after relocation
test_results.note: Chrome for Testing 151 launches from the new cache location

test_results.name: Free disk space
test_results.note: 745 MB free (~93% used). Enough to run, but low; see notes

notes: IMPORTANT: the storage volume has filesystem corruption — the kernel logged 200+ disk errors during diagnosis. Some damaged folders cannot be deleted at all, and about 6 GB of disk is 'used' but belongs to no readable file. That space can only be reclaimed by running a disk check from the host side, which I cannot do from inside the container. Please contact support to schedule a volume repair (fsck) or volume replacement.
The corruption is likely what caused the disk to fill in the first place — space from deleted files was never returned.
Disk usage is still high (~93%). If it fills again, the same agent error will return until the volume is repaired.
The MySQL service is currently stopped. Qase stores its data in files, so the app works, but anything needing the database will fail until it is started again.
review_checklist: Start a new agent run in Qase — it should now launch instead of failing with the 'no space left on device' error
Confirm the app's pages (runs, findings, bugs) still load normally
Watch disk usage; if the agent error returns, the volume repair becomes urgent
